common_statement_groups.finding: Both sources identify preview status; retain dated product context, not a project requirement.
Both identify changeability; neither establishes future stable behavior.
Both describe local macOS/Windows applicability; no universal platform or remote-session assertion.
Both recommend specifying the desired outcome.
Both distinguish current-session approval from persistent approval, when a prompt is required.
Both describe persistent approval for future sessions; no recommendation to persist it universally.
Both permit declining or canceling requested approval.
Both instruct checking the requested application against the intended task when approval is prompted.
Both instruct checking the requested action against the intended task when approval is prompted.

scope_preserving_groups.finding: Capability summaries are not enablement mandates or independently audited atomization of every interaction primitive.
CLI command preference persistence and plugin activation differ from app settings navigation; app also offers the session command. Preserve each entry point and side effect.

CLI explicitly describes organization block reporting and non-overridable local preference. The app how-to's silence is not permission to bypass managed policy; concept-page evidence must be reconciled separately.

Accessibility and Screen Recording remain separate macOS permissions. App explains purpose, recheck and granted-state display; CLI troubleshooting specifically names the helper. Do not collapse declared prerequisites into effective grants.
CLI permission mode/status and app Tool Permissions/Sessions settings are distinct control surfaces. No setting was inspected or changed.

CLI status includes skills while app status names plugin/MCP. CLI disablement verification and separate plugin/connectivity diagnosis are extra scope; none proves completed work or correct target access.

CLI describes saved approval sharing to app and deny precedence. App describes grants originating in either surface, individual removal and future-only effects; retain same-computer scope and non-revocation of existing session grants.
CLI uses two Escape presses; app uses Stop or one Escape. These are interruption variants, not interchangeable shortcuts. App separately requires session termination for session-grant revocation.
Feature disablement has command and settings routes. Neither cited off/toggle instruction establishes deletion of saved grants or revocation of all current-session permissions.
CLI unavailability and absent app settings have account/platform checks, with CLI additionally requiring local-session confirmation. Preserve failure context rather than infer a successful fallback.

generalization_proposals.proposal: Define the authorized target application, action, outcome and constraints; distinguish current-session and persistent grants and keep explicit denial effective.
generalization_proposals.applicability: Only consumers using desktop-agent capabilities; human approval boundaries remain separate
generalization_proposals.required_evidence: Actual scoped permission state and accountable task authorization, not a command string or settings-file existence

generalization_proposals.proposal: Model interruption, saved-grant removal, feature disablement and session termination as separate operations with separate postconditions.
generalization_proposals.applicability: Adapt per supported client/OS; keep both CLI and app interruption variants
generalization_proposals.required_evidence: Positive and negative runtime observations for each intended postcondition; no mutation without applicable approval

generalization_proposals.proposal: Resolve effective organization/enterprise policy before local capability enablement.
generalization_proposals.applicability: Organization-managed consumers; solo profiles still require local task authorization
generalization_proposals.required_evidence: Effective policy readback, including unavailable/permission-denied outcomes as unresolved rather than PASS

generalization_proposals.proposal: Check actual OS-helper permissions and component status separately, and do not equate enabled components with successful operation.
generalization_proposals.applicability: OS-specific prerequisite adapters, not a universal macOS rule
generalization_proposals.required_evidence: Correct helper identity and actual effective grants/connectivity on the scoped target
